plan: My value is $19. To maximize profit, I should bid below my value but high enough to have a chance at winning. I will consider the midpoint of possible values ($24.5) as a reference. Bidding slightly below my value, say $18.9, allows potential profit if others undervalue. This strategy balances the risk of overbidding against not winning.

Given my low private value of $3, bidding aggressively is not profitable. I should bid conservatively, aiming to avoid winning while still considering the possibility of others bidding low. A bid slightly below the midpoint of possible values, such as $10, minimizes the risk of overpaying if the others bid very low. This ensures minimal loss if I accidentally win, as the third-highest bid will likely be low.
